Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week — Medicore is excited about Redwood's latency and multiregion options. Procurement asked me to loop you in to put together a mutual action plan (MAP) and confirm the purchase path for an AWS Private Offer. A few things procurement needs clarified before we can issue a PO: 

- Can Redwood accept a Private Offer through the AWS Marketplace with a Net30 PO from our side (we usually push invoices through AWS Billing)?
- We require SOC 2 evidence and an audit log sample (sec team will need the artifacts).
- Timeline target: we want production access by Dec 1; pilot timeframe is Nov 8–Nov 30.

Please send a short MAP with milestones, the attachments procurement needs, and your recommended billing path. Also confirm who at Redwood will sign the Private Offer and where the DocuSign will come from.

Thanks,
Amara Singh
Director, IT Procurement
Medicore Health

Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement path — next steps

Hi Amara — great to hear and thanks for the clear ask. I pulled together a one-page MAP and a short checklist outlining what procurement will need to complete the AWS Private Offer flow. Drafts attached. High-level answers below and then a proposed milestone timeline.

Quick answers:
- AWS Private Offer: yes, we support an AWS Private Offer. The typical flow we recommend is: Redwood creates the private offer in the Marketplace, Medicore accepts it in your AWS account, then procurement issues the PO to AWS.
- Net30: customers usually route purchase through AWS Billing; we can coordinate to accept Net30 if your finance team will generate a PO to AWS (we do not take direct Net30 invoices for Marketplace purchases unless routed via partner-managed billing). If you need Redwood to invoice directly, we can discuss a parallel direct-billing SOW but that will change the procurement path.
- SOC 2 / audit artifacts: attached SOC 2 letter and an anonymized audit-log sample. Marcus (cc) will own security artifacts and can provide additional evidence if needed.

Proposed milestones (draft MAP):
- Oct 20: Legal redlines returned (Medicore legal)
- Oct 21: Redwood submits Private Offer to AWS marketplace
- Oct 22–25: AWS validation window
- Oct 28: Medicore issues PO to AWS / accept Private Offer
- Nov 1: Provisioning complete (staging)
- Nov 8: Pilot start
- Dec 1: Production go-live

Next steps from our side: I can prepare a DocuSign-ready SOW and the AWS Private Offer package once we confirm the SOW/pricing. Could you confirm who in your finance team will sign the PO and whether they require Redwood to be the invoice recipient or prefer AWS marketplace invoicing?

Thanks — attaching: Medicore_MAP_v1.pdf, AWS_PrivateOffer_Instructions.pdf, Redwood_SOC2_letter.pdf

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[evelyn_hart@redwood.com] | +1 (415) 555-0192

Evelyn — thanks for the fast turnaround and the artifacts. A couple clarifications from procurement and cloud ops: 

- Procurement confirms they will issue a PO to AWS for the Private Offer (preferred). They asked whether any line-item or contract reference Redwood needs included on the PO to ensure AWS links to the Private Offer. If so, please provide an exact contract title/reference.
- CloudOps (Michael) wrote: when Medicore accepts the Private Offer in our AWS account, how long until the account can access the private images/AMIs and the provisioning API? We need estimates to lock down the Nov 1 provisioning date.
- Legal wants to see the SOW and the Master Subscription Agreement redline prior to Oct 20. Can you route DocuSign for the SOW and specify who will be signing on Redwood's side?

Also cc'ing our billing contact (procure@medicore.com) — they will confirm if any internal billing code is needed on the PO.

Best,
Amara

Subject: RE: Medicore MAP & AWS Private Offer — legal/billing notes

Evelyn — looping in with legal and billing guidance to make the MAP actionable. Key notes for the thread and for Amara: 

1) Private Offer PO reference: provide this text to the buyer on the PO to ensure AWS links correctly — "Redwood Inference Private Offer: RW-PO-MD-1327". That exact string should be on the PO reference field.

2) Net30 billing via AWS Marketplace: AWS typically invoices the buyer; we can support the buyer's Net30 through AWS Billing (no change needed) as long as the PO references the Private Offer above. If Medicore instead requests Redwood to invoice directly, we will need a direct-billing addendum (we can prepare but that will add ~5 business days).

3) DocuSign / signatory: Redwood will sign the SOW from our authorized signatory (Laura Bennett, Head of Legal Operations). Laura (cc) will review the MSA redline and the SOW; we aim to turn redlines within 48 hours of receipt.

4) CloudOps provisioning timeline (answer to Michael): once Medicore accepts the Private Offer and AWS confirms the purchase, provisioning access is typically available within 24–72 hours for marketplace entitlements. For reserved capacity + VPC setup we'll align timelines separately but expect staging access by Nov 1 if the PO is issued by Oct 28.

I've attached an internal PO-Acceptance-Checklist and a short note for procurement with the exact PO wording. Evelyn — if you're ready, send the MAP with the PO reference string and Laura will push the DocuSign envelope when redlines come in.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: PO-Acceptance-Checklist.pdf
